strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: workspace.write can propose and proposal.apply can execute one approved patch_file operation with 2 to 5 hunks on one existing regular UTF-8 workspace file.

Multi-hunk patch apply requires WriteWorkspace permission, current unconsumed approval, expected target hash, fresh preflight, safe path validation, symlink rejection, aggregate hunk fingerprint matching, and exact non-overlapping context matching before mutation.

Proposal and apply evidence stores bounded hunk count and aggregate hunk fingerprint, not raw hunk text, raw file content, raw diffs, absolute paths, environment, prompts, provider responses, or secrets.
A headless caller can apply a cohesive multi-location single-file edit atomically without full-file replacement or sequential one-hunk races.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances controlled_workspace_tools with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: One authorized proposal.apply call can atomically apply 2 to 5 approved patch_file hunks to one existing regular UTF-8 file.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M25.1 applies one hunk only; replace_file requires full replacement content and does not provide bounded multi-location hunk admission.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie cannot perform cohesive multi-location single-file edits through one Rust-owned approval, hash, context, and ledger boundary.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M25.1 handled one patch hunk; M24.2 recovered delete transactions; M24.1 executed delete transactions. This phase adds bounded multi-hunk patch execution.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. This extends existing workspace.write proposal generation and proposal.apply execution.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. This reuses existing proposal, preflight, apply result, and ledger evidence surfaces with aggregate hunk metadata.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime validates a bounded hunk list, records an aggregate hunk fingerprint, checks all approved hunks at apply time, rejects overlapping or stale contexts, performs atomic replacement, and verifies post-write SHA-256.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless automation can execute realistic small code edits deterministically without raw ledger scraping, external patch application, or sequential one-hunk races.
answers.milestone_progress: This establishes M26's core controlled multi-hunk patch execution capability and should make the milestone eligible for closeout after review.

review_value_gate.review_intent: M26.1 must be reviewed for actual multi-hunk patch_file mutation behavior, aggregate hunk fingerprint binding, overlapping context rejection, expected hash validation, atomic replacement, post-write verification, and bounded evidence.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M26.1 changes the current phase manifest only; guard engine changes are not expected.

exit_criteria: workspace.write accepts operation=patch_file with workspace-relative path, hunks array of 2 to 5 old_text/new_text entries, and no content
Multi-hunk proposals validate an existing regular non-symlink UTF-8 target and require every old_text to match exactly once without overlap
Proposal evidence stores hunk_count and aggregate hunk_fingerprint without raw hunk text or raw file content
proposal.apply accepts approved current unconsumed multi-hunk patch_file proposals through the existing RPC only
Apply requires authorize=true, expected_target_sha256, patch_hunks, latest preflight, safe path, regular non-symlink UTF-8 target, and approved aggregate hunk metadata match
Missing, duplicate, overlapping, stale, sensitive, hash-mismatched, unsupported, unauthorized, or permission-denied patch apply attempts do not mutate the workspace or consume authorization
Successful apply writes through the existing temporary sibling and atomic replacement path, verifies post-write SHA-256, consumes authorization, and records bounded apply result evidence
Ledger and RPC results do not expose raw file content, raw diffs, raw hunk text, prompts, provider responses, stdout/stderr, environment, secrets, absolute paths, or canonical paths
next_phase_candidate_notes: After M26.1 merges, close M26 unless stale-context recovery is accepted as a distinct runtime behavior capability. Do not add report, history, digest, preview, or inspection-only wrappers.
